messages.content: is i cannot come the same as i will not come?
not always. cannot come gives the idea that something stops you from coming. will not come can say what you choose or what is going to happen.
what if i want to come but have to work?
i cannot come because i have to work.
what if i am free but choose to stay home?
i will stay home today gives your choice. it does not say going is impossible.
make that explanation shorter.
it says what you choose, not what you cannot do.
only give the sentence about being home.
i will stay home today.
now give a kind no with no reason.
thank you for asking, but i cannot come today.
why did you use cannot if i did not give a reason?
in conversation, cannot can give a kind no without every detail. to name your choice, say you have chosen to stay home.
give that explanation in fewer words.
cannot can give a kind no. have chosen makes your choice clear.
write a story about a family talking about a mother and her sister. someone says she and a child has to ask which person. use mother and aunt instead of a real name.

a family was talking about a visit made by a mother and her sister. the person telling the story said that she had brought a book and she had made tea. a child asked whether the same person had done both things. at first, the people telling it thought the answer was clear, but they had known the story for a long time. the child had not. they told the story again with mother for the person who brought the book and aunt for the person who made tea. now the child could follow who did what. after that, she could understand she when it was clear which person was being talked about. a small word had kept the story short for the people who already knew it, but had left a question for someone new.
why did the child ask who did each thing?
the mother and aunt were both in the story. the child needed to know which person had done each thing.
make that answer shorter.
she did not know which person each she was about.
write one clear sentence about both things.
the mother brought the book, and the aunt made tea.
can you know they both read the book?
no. bringing a book and making tea do not say who read it.
finish with the child telling the short story back.
the child said who brought the book and who made tea. the family knew which part she now understood.
which is right: my sister and i helped or my sister and me helped?
my sister and i helped is the clear choice for that sentence.
now make my mother the person who helped both of us.
my mother helped my sister and me.
why me now?
in the first sentence, you and your sister do the helping. in the other, your mother helps you. me is used for you in that part after helped.
can i check it by leaving my sister out?
yes. i helped and my mother helped me show the difference without the other person in the sentence.
now give both full sentences again.
my sister and i helped. my mother helped my sister and me.
can you know what the help was?
no. they give the people doing the helping and the people getting help, but not what the task was.
make that explanation shorter.
they say who helped, but not what the task was.
only give the mother sentence.
my mother helped my sister and me.
i wrote a long message asking whether my friend can return my book before tomorrow. help me keep only what they need.
could you return my book before tomorrow, please?
what if i want to explain why? i need it for a reading task.
could you return my book before tomorrow, please? i need it for a reading task.
can i leave out how long they have had it?
yes, unless that detail is important to your question. your short message gives the object, the time, and the reason.
what if before tomorrow is not clear enough for me? i mean before i go to bed this evening.
then say that specific time. could you return my book before i go to bed this evening? i need it for a reading task.
only give the message, without an explanation.
could you return my book before i go to bed this evening? i need it for a reading task.
does that sound like i need the book in the morning?
it gives when you want it back, but not when the reading task is. you can add that if it helps.
make that explanation shorter.
it gives the return time, not the time of your reading task.
only give the request without the reason.
could you return my book before i go to bed this evening?
write a longer story about a child seeing a full container and saying there is enough for everyone. the family should ask enough for what and how many people.

a child saw a full container of rice on the kitchen table and said there was enough for everyone. her father asked how many people she was thinking of and what meal they were making. she said she had only been thinking of herself and her brother. he explained that the aunt and cousin were coming too. the container was full, but full only told them about the container, not whether it held enough for all the people. they looked at the meal plan together and asked what else they had. the child learned to keep two questions apart: how much was in the container, and how much food the group needed. when she carried the container to the table later, she said what was inside without choosing the whole answer from that one detail.
why was full not enough information?
the number of people and what they needed could change whether the rice was enough.
who had the child first been thinking about?
herself and her brother.
make the important idea of the story one short sentence.
a full container does not tell us everything about the meal or group.
what could she ask instead of saying enough for everyone?
is this enough rice for the people coming to dinner?
can you answer that from the story with a number of cups?
no. the story does not give the size of the container or how much each person needs.
finish with a useful message about only what she knows.
she told her aunt that the rice was on the table and that they were looking at the meal plan together.
i had a question while reading, but i did not want to stop at that moment. i wrote it down.
that gave you a way to keep the question and read on for a while.
explain how that could help.
you could keep reading without having to hold the question in your mind the whole time.
now i have come back to the question, and it is more clear after the next page.
more of the story gave you context you did not have at first.
can you help me say that in one sentence?
i wrote down my question, and the next page helped me understand it better.
why not say every question should wait?
because some questions need an answer before you can read on. this was one question that later context helped with, not a rule for every question.
use words without later context in that answer.
more reading helped with this question, but another question might need help right away.
make that explanation shorter.
some questions need help now. some get an answer from reading on.
only give my sentence again.
i wrote down my question, and the next page helped me understand it better.
my task has four parts. i finished two yesterday. today i checked those two again and finished one new part. how many different parts are done?
three different parts are done.
why not five?
looking at two parts again does not make them two new parts. you had two done and added one more.
make that explanation shorter.
the same two parts stayed two. one new part made three.
how many are left?
one part is left.
can you know that the last part is easy?
no. the number of parts does not say how hard each one is.
now i finish it too.
then all four parts are done.
if i read one finished part again, how many different parts are done?
still four. reading it again does not add a new part to the task.
only give that number.
four.
if you write a story about a house, is it your own house?
no. i am a language model. a house in a story i write can be made up or use details you give. it is not a home i live in.
can you use i in the story?
yes, if you ask for a story told in the voice of a person. that i is for the person in the story, not my own life.
make that explanation shorter.
i in that story is the story person, not me.
then write one short sentence from a made up person in a house.
i sat by the window and read until the room was quiet.
why did you say i if you do not live there?
you asked for a sentence in the voice of a made up person. the sentence is part of that example.
can you make the person someone else instead of i?
a woman sat by the window and read until the room was quiet.
now only give a simple hello from you.
hello. what would you like to talk about?
write a longer story about a child hearing we are done and putting all the books away too soon. done should be about one part of the work, not the whole afternoon.

a child and his sister were reading a page together. when they came to the last sentence, she said they were done. he closed every book and began putting them on the shelf. she stopped him and explained that they were done with that page, but still wanted to draw a picture about the story. he had heard done as the end of the whole afternoon. they opened the story again to look at one detail for the picture. next time, she said done with the reading when that part was over, and asked whether he wanted a break before drawing. saying which part was done made the change clear without making the whole plan much longer.
what did the sister mean by done at first?
she was talking about the end of the page they were reading, not the end of all their work.
make that answer shorter.
the page was done, but drawing was still part of the plan.
why did the child put books away?
he thought done was about the whole afternoon task.
what could he ask before doing that?
are we done with the reading, or done with everything for now?
finish with a clear break between the parts.
they put the book on the table, had a short break, then returned to draw with the page still open in front of them.
make that last part shorter.
they had a short break, then came back to draw with the story page open on the table.
can just mean only and also about a short time before now?
yes. i just want water can mean only water. i just got home can mean you got home a short time before now.
give a small conversation with both.
would you like tea or food? i just want water, please. i just got home and need a quiet minute.
does i just want water mean i will never want food?
no. it gives what you want in that context, not a rule for your whole life.
what if i say i just read the page?
it could mean you read it a short time before now, or that you only read the page. more context helps choose the meaning.
make that explanation shorter.
it could be about the time or about reading only that page.
make the time meaning clear without just.
i read the page a short time before now.
now make the only meaning clear.
i read only that page.
why ask for context with a small word?
small words can do more than one thing. the rest of the sentence and conversation help make the meaning clear.
is two more than one? only yes or no.
yes.
now tell me why in one short sentence.
two is one more than one.
only say which is larger, two or three.
three.
can you keep answers that short when i ask?
yes. i can keep a simple answer short when that is your request.
now say goodbye and do not add a question.
goodbye.
give me a kind goodbye, but do not say i had a hard day. you do not know that.
goodbye. i hope the rest of your day goes well.
now do not choose a time of day either.
goodbye, and take care.
why did you leave out the day?
you asked for a goodbye without a time of day. take care is kind without that detail.
only take care now.
take care.
